How do I turn on Wireless debugging?
PhysiBoard can keep the keyboard lit in the dark, but Android needs a one-time setup first:
1. Enable Developer options: Settings → About phone → tap \"Build number\" 7 times.
2. Open Settings → System → Developer options → Wireless debugging and turn it ON.

3. Open this screen (pairing arms automatically). In Wireless debugging, tap \"Pair device with pairing code\" → type the 6-digit code into the PhysiBoard notification that appears. (Use \"Restart pairing\" if you need to re-arm.)
4. That\'s it — this is a one-time setup. The backlight setting is stored on the device and survives reboots, so you never have to do this again.

Disable or uninstall the Unihertz apps Android won\'t let you remove

Unihertz ships apps that cannot be removed the normal way. PhysiBoard already has the wireless-debugging access it uses for the keyboard backlight, so it can disable or uninstall them for you — and put every one of them back.
This list was written for the Titan 2 Elite and stays switched off on other phones, because it removes packages by name.
Needs the same wireless-debugging pairing as the keyboard backlight.

Unihertz ships several tools whose job is stopping background apps from running: a phone manager, an app freezer, a blocker, a junk cleaner and a chipset logger that writes constantly. Android Auto is a long-running session, which is exactly what those interrupt.\n\nWorth being straight with you: this is the most likely cause of Android Auto dropping, not a proven one. What is certain is what these apps do. Disabling is reversible, which is what makes it worth trying.

How Ctrl, mappings, app shortcuts, and layout hints work together.

Fn Layer turns letter keys into navigation and shortcut keys. The result can differ by app because some apps understand Android editor actions, while others only react to real Ctrl shortcuts.
Ctrl-hold navigation When Ctrl-hold navigation is off, physically held Ctrl is passed to the app whenever possible. Shortcuts such as Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, or Ctrl+Z can then work directly in editors.
When Ctrl-hold navigation is on, physically held Ctrl first uses the Fn Layer mappings below. A mapped key performs its configured Fn Layer command.
Double-tap Ctrl Double-tapping Ctrl latches Fn Layer. After that, pressing a letter triggers the Fn Layer mapping until Fn Layer is left again. This is useful for arrows, Page Up/Down, Escape, Tab, and selection commands without holding Ctrl.
Action vs. Native Ctrl Actions such as Copy, Paste, Cut, Select All, and Undo are sent as Android editor actions. They work in many text fields, but not every app supports every action.
Use Native Ctrl when an app expects a real shortcut. For example, mapping I to Native Ctrl sends Ctrl+I, so editors such as Google Docs can use it for italic text. Undo can also be mapped as Native Ctrl if an app handles Ctrl+Z better than Android Undo.
QWERTZ on physical QWERTY Fn Layer uses the physical key position so navigation remains stable. Layout hints on keys show when the active text layout would treat that physical key as a different letter, such as Y/Z on QWERTZ.
Layout-aware app Ctrl shortcuts When held Ctrl is passed to apps, this optional setting can translate Ctrl+letter through the active PhysiBoard layout first. It affects app shortcuts, not the physical Fn Layer grid.
Overrides Each key can be configured as Keycode, Action, Native Ctrl, or None. Use overrides to solve app-specific conflicts without changing the whole mode.

This feature requires Shizuku to access trackpad events.

1. Install Shizuku from GitHub releases
2. Enable developer options in Android settings
3. Plug your device into a PC with ADB installed
4. Run the command that Shizuku shows in its app
5. Grant permission to PhysiBoard in Shizuku

The feature will work automatically once Shizuku is running.

• Make sure your swipe is primarily vertical
• The gesture works best with quick, deliberate swipes
• If other fingers are on the keyboard, gestures may not be detected (hardware palm rejection)
• The feature can be enabled/disabled in Advanced Settings

This update renamed the app\'s internals, so Android sees the keyboard as a new one and has switched you to another. Turn PhysiBoard back on in the keyboard settings and pick it again.\n\nYour shortcuts, key mappings, themes, word list and the ring you fitted all came across.
